name: Durable per-person memory: 'remember this' is saved to that parent's own notes and found again
description: A parent texts 'remember that...' and their own agent writes the fact to its notes and finds it again in later chats. Whether a saved note survives the next deploy depends on one open decision about where those notes live.
example: Jordan texts: 'Remember that piano moved to Thursdays at 4.' A week later she asks 'which day is piano?' and gets Thursday at 4.
how:
Allow write/edit (deny apply_patch) on

-main with rw workspace; in-house before_tool_call hook limits paths to MEMORY.md, USER.md, memory/*.md; memory_search FTS-only; session-memory hook.
caveats: The family-facts generator renders into the same MEMORY.md and USER.md (F042), and F042 expects a chat edit to a generated file to be lost on the next deploy. Whether the generator keeps lines Happy saved by chat was not checked, so either it preserves a hand-written section or chat-saved notes go to memory/*.md only. The second choice has a cost: MEMORY.md is in context from the start of a chat, while of the dated notes only today's and yesterday's load at a fresh start and older ones are found only when the agent searches (memory.md:22, memory-architecture.md:54). Until this is settled, a saved note is not guaranteed to survive a deploy.
Search is by keyword only until local embeddings are added (F046), so a saved note is found by its words, not by its meaning.

MEMORY.md is loaded at the start of a parent's one-to-one chat but not in scheduled jobs, group chats or hand-offs to a helper (user-model.md:376), so a brief or a reminder does not know a saved note unless its job is given memory search.

The planned refusal of memory writes in a turn that carried web or research results is not something the platform does for a file write. OpenClaw does mark the rest of a turn as tainted once a tool result declares web content, and classifies memory from that turn as untrusted (memory-architecture.md:117), but the docs opened describe this as a label used for promotion and for loading, and their advice for preventing a write is to restrict the file tools (memory-provenance.md:182). No taint flag that a hook can read was found, so the hook would have to track web tool calls itself. Untested.
Notes belong to one parent. Something both parents should get the same answer to belongs in the household store (F031) or the family handbook (F043).
Later option if saved notes and search prove too weak: Active Memory's recall across conversations, which adds a blocking model call to each reply it runs on.
corrections: The catalog relies on `sessions_search` with visibility `agent` to find pre-reset conversations. docs/gateway/config-tools/sessions-and-subagents.md:58 says a sandboxed session stays limited to sessions it spawned while agents.defaults.sandbox.sessionToolsVisibility is 'spawned' (the default); the mains run with sandbox mode all, so that key must change as well. docs/tools/multi-agent-sandbox-tools.md:372 adds that tools.sessions.visibility is gateway-wide, not per agent.
unverified: Whether visibility 'self' already reaches the same chat's pre-reset history (the docs define self as the current session key) was not tested.

No taint flag that a plugin hook can read was found in the hook docs opened, although OpenClaw's memory design does mark a turn as tainted after web content (memory-architecture.md:117); so 'refuse writes after web results' means the hook tracking web tool calls itself. Untested.

How OpenClaw classifies a MEMORY.md that the agent edited directly is not stated in the docs opened. It loads MEMORY.md and USER.md at the start of a chat only when their provenance counts as eligible (memory-architecture.md:215), so check on a live turn that a note saved right after a web search does not stop the file from loading.
Whether the F042 generator keeps lines Happy saved by chat was not checked; the generator was not opened.
safety: Each parent's notes stay in that parent's own agent, and shared agents such as research hold no memory. Writes are limited to the memory files by a before_tool_call hook, which fails closed, and apply_patch is denied by name. A saved note is also where an injected instruction could persist, so the plan is to refuse memory writes in a turn that carried web or research results; the hook has to track that itself and this is untested. The weekly review of what Happy did and remembered (G006) shows each adult what was saved.

name: Family facts, standing preferences and reply language rendered into each parent's agent from family.json5
description: Both parents' agents start every chat already knowing the kids' school, routines and activities and each adult's standing preferences, including the language to reply in. On request Happy also turns a school note into a short Chinese text a parent can forward to a grandparent.
example: Jordan writes to Happy in Chinese and is answered in Chinese; Tony texts 'put this school note in Chinese for grandma' and gets three short lines to forward.
how: One generator, one file. From family.json5 the generator renders each adult's directives into USER.md (4,000-character cap), the per-person reply-language line among them (G011), and the kid and routine facts into MEMORY.md with trigger comments (F042); nothing is rendered into shared agents. Scheduled jobs do not read that line, so the language is written into each job message. The grandparent version is a prompt-only request on the parent's own agent: no new tool and no send path, and the parent forwards the text.
caveats: USER.md has a 4,000-character cap that all standing preferences share, so the list has to stay short.

Rendered facts change only when the family file is edited and redeployed, and a chat edit to a generated file is expected to be lost on the next deploy; things a parent says in chat go through the memory write path (F041).

On supported iPhones Messages can already translate a conversation automatically and on device, so plain back-and-forth with a grandparent may need nothing from Happy; whether that covers Chinese on this family's phones is not confirmed.
Happy's distinct part on the language side is the shortened Chinese version of a school note, and its translation quality for school notices was not evaluated.

A per-language voice switch is documented only for the bundled Microsoft speech provider, which is an online service, so it does not help the offline say path, and whether the default say voice pronounces Chinese was not tested.
The generator script and the family registry were not opened in this review.
corrections: A 9 Oct verifier note says there is no per-language voice switch. tts/output.md:56 documents one for the bundled Microsoft provider, which is an online service; it does not help the offline say path.
unverified: The generator script and the family registry live in happy-config and were not opened in this run.
That a chat edit to a generated file is lost on the next deploy is a property of Tony's generator, not something an opened source states.
Translation quality into Chinese by gpt-6-sol for school notices was not evaluated.
Which iPhone models and languages Apple's Live Translation covers for this family was not confirmed; the Apple page defers to an availability list.
Whether the macOS say default voice pronounces Chinese text was not tested.
safety: The rendered files hold the children's school and routines, so they go only into the two parents' own agents and never into shared agents such as research, the group agent or the mail readers. No tool and no send path are added; a translated note leaves the family only when a parent forwards it.

name: Household knowledge vault: shared family handbook, including the home systems and service-provider registry
description: One shared family handbook that both parents' agents can search: people, home systems, providers, renewal dates, sitter notes. A photo of an appliance's data plate, sent once, fills in the home-systems page, so a later 'what filter does the furnace take?' or 'who fixed the boiler?' gets the stored answer.
example: Tony sends a photo of the furnace data plate and texts 'save this'. A month later Jordan asks: 'What filter does the furnace take?'
how: Step 1 (F043): a shared Markdown folder added to each main's `memory.search.extraPaths`. Step 2: enable the bundled memory-wiki plugin with `vault.scope` global and its own vault directory; `wiki_search`, `wiki_get`, `wiki_apply` and `wiki_lint` on the two mains only. Registry (F034): with inbound attachments on, the vision model reads the data plate and the agent saves a wiki synthesis page with `wiki_apply`, or a fact in the household store; manuals given as a link go through the research agent. With only step 1 in place, the operator types the plate details into the folder by hand.
caveats: The two installed pages disagree on whether enabling memory-wiki needs a gateway restart.
That memory_search in a sandboxed main can read a shared folder outside its workspace was not tested.
Saving a data plate as a wiki page needs step 2; with only the shared folder the operator types the details in by hand.
Data-plate photos go to the cloud vision model, which is the attachments decision recorded under F002, and image input on the family's custom provider ids was not re-checked.
The vault is shared by design, so both parents' agents search and edit the same pages.

Other entries file into it: the renewals look-ahead keeps a policy's one-line summary page here, and a pet's vet contact and food reorder link would sit in the provider registry, with nothing ordered.
unverified: The two installed pages disagree on whether enabling memory-wiki needs a gateway restart (docs/plugins/memory-wiki.md:26 says it applies to a running gateway, docs/cli/wiki.md:15 shows a restart).
That memory_search in a sandboxed main can read a shared folder outside its workspace was not tested.
That gpt-6-sol accepts images on Tony's custom provider ids was not checked in this run.
The memory-wiki route needs that bundled plugin enabled (F043 step 2); with only the shared Markdown folder, the operator types the plate details in by hand.
safety: Vault pages are private family data and stay on the two parents' own agents, which have no browse tool; the research agent that reads manuals holds none of it. A data-plate photo is untrusted content read by an agent with memory, but that agent can reply only to its owner or, once family delivery exists, the family.

name: Teach Happy a routine (operator-reviewed skills), with a parent-run practice quiz as the first skill
description: A parent describes once how the family does something (party plan, ski-trip packing, school-form explainer); Tony turns it into a named skill, and after the next deploy Happy can load it when a later request fits the skill's one-line description. The first skill is a practice quiz that a parent runs from a study-guide photo, a pasted spelling list or a request for math facts: ten questions, one at a time, hint first, a running score and the answer key at the end.
example: 'Happy, learn our ski-trip packing routine: ask how many nights and who is coming, then list by person, and always include the kids' helmets.' Or Jordan sends a photo of the science study guide and texts: 'quiz us on this, 10 questions, one at a time.'
how:
Pipeline (AUT-06): Happy answers with the drafted procedure as plain text; Tony turns it into `skills//SKILL.md` in happy-config, reviews it, and happy-deploy copies it into that agent's workspace `skills/` folder. The model loads a skill by reading its SKILL.md, so `

-main` needs `read` in `tools.alsoAllow` and the sandbox tool allowlist; `skill_workshop` stays denied on every family agent. A routine of a few lines can live in AGENTS.md instead. Quiz (MKT-02): one such skill fixes the format (one question per message, one hint before revealing, a running score, the answer key at the end, no web lookups); a photo needs attachment intake (F002) and is read by the reply model's own vision; an optional one-shot reminder offers a re-quiz the night before.
depends_on: a skills step in happy-deploy and gen-family
automatic self-learning switched off in config (`skills.workshop.autonomous.mode: "off"`)
decision: who may request a new skill

`read` allowed on

-main in tools.alsoAllow and the sandbox tool allowlist (group:fs is denied today; arrives with F041)
F002 photo and PDF reading with inbound attachments switched on, for the quiz's photo route only

F007 automations tool on

-main, only for the optional re-quiz reminder
F003 voice over iMessage, its local spoken replies, only for reading spelling words aloud
caveats: Asking Happy to save a skill from iMessage does not work on this stack: sandboxed runs do not construct the `skill_workshop` tool, and the documented exception would publish with no pending draft and so skip Tony's review, which is one more reason to keep that tool off every family agent.
A skill is know-how: it cannot add tools or accounts, so 'learn to order the groceries' still ends at a list.

A skill is instruction text loaded into future sessions, so one written from a pasted web page or an email is a stored injection: author only from the parent's own words, and install no marketplace skills (an audit reported by The Hacker News found 341 malicious entries among 2,857 ClawHub skills in early 2026).

Turnaround is 'when Tony next deploys', and Happy does not run a skill every time: the prompt lists only each skill's name and one-line description, so that line has to be precise, and calling the skill by name (`/skill <name>`) is the sure route where that command is accepted from the sender.

The quiz is parent-run only: the kids are not users, the parent holds the phone and sends the answers, and a version a child uses alone waits for the kids agent (F072) and never uses a cloud model or cloud speech.

The ChatGPT or Gemini app on a parent's phone already makes a quiz from uploaded material, with hints and an end summary; Happy's only edge is that it lives in the same thread and can schedule the re-quiz.
Models write wrong answer keys, especially for arithmetic and for facts the sheet does not state, so tell it to quiz only from what is on the page and spot-check.

A text quiz shows spelling words on screen, so spelling practice needs the words read aloud with the local voice (F003), whose quality for spelling words is untried, and the running score lives in the conversation and is gone after the daily session reset.
safety: Operator review is the gate: no model-written file reaches a skills root, and a skill cannot widen tool policy. The quiz is the riskier part: a photographed school worksheet is untrusted content, is not screened by the PDF privacy gate in F002, and goes to the cloud vision model under store:false. No child's account talks to a cloud model.
unverified: Whether a user-invocable skill command typed by an allowlisted non-owner iMessage sender is accepted on 2026.9.7.
That skill sync into the sandbox works with `workspaceAccess: "none"` (the docs say sandboxed runs read materialized copies).

That a `read`-only grant on a sandboxed

-main reaches the mirrored skills and nothing private; check at build time.
Whether an iMessage owner turn is ever given library-authoring authority on this configuration. If it is, an allowlisted `skill_workshop` could publish a skill with no review.
Whether a spoken reply arrives as a playable voice message or as a file in iMessage Basic mode.
The quality of the macOS say voice for spelling words was not tried.

name: Semantic memory search with local embeddings (text only)
description: Search notes by meaning ('the kid's nut thing' finds 'tree-nut allergy') with embeddings computed on the Mac mini; photo search stays unavailable locally.
example: Jordan asks: 'What was the kid's nut thing again?' The note that says 'tree-nut allergy' comes back, although none of the words match.
how: Install @openclaw/llama-cpp-provider, run the embedding-only setup, set memory.search.provider local with fallback none, reindex; image indexing still requires gemini-embedding-2 (cloud).
caveats: For a few hundred family notes keyword search may already find most things; how much better search by meaning would be here is a judgement, not a measured figure.
Photos and audio cannot be searched this way on the Mac mini: on this version image and audio indexing works only with Google's cloud embedding model.
If the embedding server on the Mac mini fails, search drops back to keyword matching without telling the parent; the reason shows only in a debug field.
corrections: The catalog ties this to M2 (local models). docs/plugins/llama-cpp.md:123 documents an embedding-only setup that adds no chat model, so the text leg does not depend on M2 and can be done on the installed stack.

The 9 Oct reason for dropping photo search is that no local multimodal embedder exists. Google's EmbeddingGemma page now describes EmbeddingGemma 2 as multimodal and local; the actual block is that OpenClaw 2026.9.7 only indexes images with gemini-embedding-2 (docs/reference/memory-config.md:495).
unverified: Whether the managed llama.cpp server in 2026.9.7 can load EmbeddingGemma 2 was not checked.
The gain over keyword search for a few hundred family notes is a judgement, not a sourced figure.
Whether search by meaning finds a note saved in Chinese from a question asked in English, or the reverse, was not tested; it depends on the embedding model chosen.
safety: Embeddings are computed by a server on the Mac mini with the cloud fallback set to none, so note text is not sent to an embedding service. No tool and no send path are added; it only changes how the existing memory search ranks notes.

name: Per-person read-only mail agent: 'did I get an email about X?' on request, and a 07:00 digest of mail that needs action
description: One locked-down mail agent per adult reads that adult's own Gmail under a read-only grant: a parent asks 'did the dentist confirm?' and gets the sender, the date and the gist, and at 07:00 the same agent texts about ten lines on mail that needs a reply, has a deadline or involves money (from January to April a Saturday text adds which expected tax forms have had an arrival email). Nothing in Gmail is changed, labelled, drafted or sent, and the agent cannot browse, run code or message anyone but its owner.
example: Tony texts: 'Did the dentist confirm Thursday?' and gets the sender, the date and one line of gist from his own inbox. Trigger, 07:00, text to Tony: 'Mail that needs you: the plumber asks you to confirm Thursday's visit by tomorrow; the car insurance renewal is due on 20 October. Nothing else needs a reply.'
how:
Agent (G015): one `

-mail` entry per adult with `profile: "minimal"`, an explicit `

-gmail__*` allow plus the `tools.sandbox.tools` gate, web, fs, runtime and browser denied, memory search off; checked with `openclaw sandbox explain --agent`. Tool (F047): `gog mcp` as a host-side stdio entry under `mcp.servers`, narrowed with `--allow-tool` to the Gmail read tools (its default also registers Drive, Docs, Sheets and Calendar reads); one token per adult from `gog auth add` with `--services` limited to Gmail and `--gmail-scope readonly`. Lookup: `

-main` spawns `

-mail` through `subagents.allowAgents`. Digest (F016): an isolated 07:00 job on `

-mail` with `--tools "

-gmail__*,llm-task"`, announced to the owner only; health senders by subject line only. Tax forms (F061): a Saturday job, January to April, on the same agent.
caveats: The roadmap's M4 keeps each inbox on a local model and none is installed, so the lookup and the digest both send personal mail to the cloud model, and without Zero Data Retention the 30-day abuse-monitoring log applies to that text; this is Tony's open decision and the whole card waits on it.

Google already does much of this where the mail lives: the Gemini app answers questions from a person's own Gmail and lists a daily digest of calendar, to-dos and emails among its scheduled actions, and Gmail's 'AI Inbox' was announced in January 2026, so try those on one parent's account before building; Happy adds only asking, and being told, in the iMessage thread.
gog is not installed on this Mac, so its flags come from upstream docs and must be confirmed with `gog mcp --list-tools` and `gog auth add --help` on the installed version.
With sandbox mode all, MCP tools stay hidden unless `tools.sandbox.tools` names `bundle-mcp` or the server glob, and the minimal profile does not allow MCP tools implicitly.

A Google sign-in app left in Testing issues tokens that expire after seven days, so the app is published to In production (the consent screen then shows a warning) or each adult signs in again every week; whether both adults' tokens can share one keyring under the happy user is still open.

'Send pinned to owner' applies only when the mail agent runs its own scheduled turn, because a mail agent spawned from `

-main` always loses `message` and `session_status`; that a before_tool_call hook reaches MCP tool calls is implied by the docs but not stated.
'Memory off' is not one switch: memory search has a per-agent override, dreaming is plugin-wide, and the session-exclusion setting only matches hook sessions.

Reply drafts are left out, 'subject line only for health senders' and 'do not open the form' are instructions to the agent and not enforced limits, and the tax-form check only knows that a notice email arrived, so a form that came by post or sits in a portal shows as missing.
corrections: The 9 Oct needs list omits the sandbox-layer gate: with sandbox mode 'all', MCP tools stay hidden unless `tools.sandbox.tools` names `bundle-mcp` or the server glob (docs/gateway/config-tools/tool-policy.md:101 and :130). The minimal profile does not allow MCP tools implicitly either (same file, lines 36 and 41).

'Memory off' is not one switch in the installed docs: memory search has a per-agent override (`agents.entries.*.memory.search`, `enabled`, docs/reference/memory-config.md:31 and :102), dreaming is plugin-wide (docs/concepts/memory.md:275), and `excludeSessions.hookExternalContentSources` only matches hook sessions (docs/reference/memory-config.md:667).

'Send pinned to owner' only applies when the mail agent runs its own scheduled or hook turn: when spawned from `

-main` it always loses `message` and `session_status` (docs/tools/subagents/tool-policy.md:23), so its allow list must not consist of `session_status` alone.
The 9 Oct needs list puts `openclaw models status --agent --probe` in the deploy checks; the installed doc says a direct probe needs the Gateway stopped (docs/cli/models.md:121).

The 9 Oct verifier note says gogcli has no read-only-only Gmail scope. The upstream command reference lists `--gmail-scope full|readonly|send|read-send` and says `--readonly` on `gog auth add` requests read-only OAuth scopes, so a read-only grant can be requested; the catalog's hedge 'if the installed version supports it' can be firmed up, pending a check on the installed binary.

The 9 Oct text treats the `

-gmail` wrapper as new code. Upstream gogcli ships a stdio MCP server (`gog mcp`) that exposes only read tools unless `--allow-write` is passed, so the config entry can run gog directly with an `--allow-tool` list and no wrapper.

The 9 Oct needs list stops at the per-agent allow list. With sandbox mode 'all' (Happy's setting) the installed docs add a second gate: MCP tools are filtered out unless `tools.sandbox.tools` also names `bundle-mcp` or the server glob (docs/gateway/config-tools/tool-policy.md:101 and :130).
unverified: The per-person provider setting that sends store false was verified in M1 and not re-read here.
Whether this OpenAI account has zero retention; without it the 30-day abuse-monitoring log applies to mail text sent to the model.
The promptfoo boundary canary is in-house.
A before_tool_call hook reaching MCP tool calls is implied by the doc ('every tool call in the run', docs/plugins/hooks/tool-policy.md:222) but I found no sentence naming MCP tools.
gog is not installed on this Mac; the flags come from the upstream main-branch docs and must be confirmed with `gog mcp --list-tools` and `gog auth add --help` on the version Homebrew installs.

Whether both adults' tokens would sit in one keyring under the happy user: upstream says tokens use the platform keyring by default with a file backend for headless hosts; splitting them with a per-adult GOG_HOME is my inference from the paths doc.

That publishing the self-made Google sign-in app to In production, as gog's quickstart describes, keeps a read-only Gmail token alive past seven days on a personal, unverified app was not tested; Google's scope page marks gmail.readonly as a Restricted scope.
The promptfoo injection canary is an in-house test, not an OpenClaw feature.
Whether personal mail may go to the cloud model under store:false is Tony's open decision; no source settles it.
A read-only scope flag on `gog auth add`: the opened gog pages name a runtime `--readonly` flag and a baked read-only build, not an auth-time scope flag.

Whether Gmail's AI Inbox is available on the parents' accounts in October 2026: Google's January 2026 announcement was read, and later press coverage tying it to paid Google AI plans was seen only in search results.
safety: The mail agent holds private mail and reads untrusted mail text, so it gets no way out: no web, file, code or browser tools, no draft or send tool, and texts only to the mailbox's owner. The digest runs unattended on that same agent. The open question is the model: personal mail would go to the cloud model.

name: Email me this: long answers, tables and plans sent to the asker's own inbox (owner-only mailout)
description: 'Email me this': long answers, tables and plans land in the asker's own inbox from a dedicated family sender. A hook that fails closed is meant to block any send that is not addressed to the asker alone; that block has to be proven with a test send before go-live.
example: Jordan texts: 'Email me the camp comparison.' The full table arrives in her own inbox from the family sender address; nobody else can be put on the To line.
how:
A send-only mail tool on a dedicated family sender account: the gog MCP server with the write flag plus its separate `--allow-gmail-send` flag and only the send tool allowed, granted to `

-main` only. A `before_tool_call` hook blocks the call unless the recipient equals the owner address of the calling agent and cc and bcc are empty; a block is terminal and the hook fails closed. Do not rely on rewriting the recipient: the docs describe rewrites for host-owned tool parameters only. An in-house daily send cap.
caveats: The promise that nobody else can be a recipient rests on an in-house hook, and it is not yet shown that the hook sees every recipient field (to, cc, bcc) of the send tool: a seeded send to a non-owner address must be blocked before this goes live.
The hook blocks a wrong recipient; it does not correct it, because the docs describe rewriting parameters for host-owned tools only.
It needs a dedicated family sender Google account with a send grant, set up by hand outside OpenClaw, and a daily send cap that is in-house code (no built-in cap was found).
gog's quickstart says a Google sign-in app left in Testing issues tokens that expire after seven days, so the sender account needs the app published to In production, as the mail reader (G015) does.
unverified: That the hook sees every recipient field (to, cc, bcc) of the gog MCP send tool in its parameters; prove it with a seeded send to a non-owner address, which must be blocked.
A daily send cap is in-house code; no built-in cap was found in the pages read.
Creating the dedicated family sender account and granting its send scope is a manual step outside OpenClaw.
safety: The send tool sits on each parent's own agent, which holds private data, so the recipient pin is the protection: a fail-closed hook blocks any send that is not addressed to the calling agent's owner alone, with no cc or bcc, and the tool is granted to no shared or mail-reading agent. Mail leaves from a dedicated family sender address, not from a parent's own account.

name: Kids agent (waits for a local model): text with homework hints, chat hours, parent alerts and a nightly digest, then the kitchen speaker
description: Later, each child texts Happy from their own Apple account and gets a helper with no tools and no memory, on a local model, that gives grade-level hints and short explanations and is told not to hand over a finished worksheet; the parents get chat hours per child, an immediate text when a message is flagged for safety or distress, and an evening digest of what each child asked. As a second step the same kids agent answers by voice through the roadmap's kitchen speaker (Home Assistant Voice Preview Edition), with wake word, speech-to-text and text-to-speech running locally so that only text reaches Happy.
example: Trigger: at 21:40 the 8-year-old texts the kids agent and gets a fixed 'time for bed, ask me tomorrow' line. At the kitchen speaker: 'Okay Nabu, why is the sky blue?'
how: Base (F072): `bindings[]` by DM handle to one agent per kid, the minimal profile with `session_status` and `gateway` denied, memory search off, a daily reset and an in-house kid-safety plugin with a local classifier on `before_dispatch` and `message_sending`. Hints (F073): hint-first rules and a grade band in AGENTS.md; no URLs. Hours and alerts (MKT-13): the same plugin gives a fixed reply outside each kid's hours and texts both parents the category and time on a safety label. Digest (G019): a host-side command job summarises the day's sessions on a local model. Speaker (VOX-11): the device, Home Assistant OS in a VM on the Mac, Whisper and Piper through the Wyoming integration, and a kids-only shim in front of the gateway, whose OpenAI-compatible chat endpoint is full operator access.
caveats: Blocked until a local model and local classifiers exist and the kid-safety evals pass, because kids' content never goes to a cloud model or cloud speech.

A local classifier's accuracy on how 8 and 10-year-olds actually write is unproven: false alarms will annoy, misses matter more, and a home system has no human reviewer between the flag and the parent notice.

Common Sense Media rated Google's supervised assistant for under-13s high risk and says chatbot use at ages 6 to 12 should happen only with close parent supervision and in moderation; an alert and an evening digest are a look afterwards, not supervision, so whether a child may chat alone is a decision to take before building.
'Refuse whole-worksheet answers' is a prompt rule, and no source shows a model holds to it when a child pushes.
The alert is a heads-up to parents and not a crisis service, and the parents should be told so.

The speaker has no interim adult version: nothing identifies who is speaking, so without a local model a child's question would reach OpenAI as text, and speech stays in the house only while Home Assistant's own cloud speech option is left off.

The hop from Home Assistant to Happy is unsolved: Home Assistant's official OpenAI integration only talks to OpenAI's own endpoint, and with token auth OpenClaw's chat endpoint gives the caller the full operator scope set and lets the request choose the agent, so the bridge would be a community integration or a self-written kids-only shim.

The speaker adds an always-on VM to patch and back up, Home Assistant itself calls the device a preview, and open-ended questions need Whisper, which Home Assistant recommends only on powerful hardware.
corrections: 'OpenAI terms are 13+, no cloud shortcut' could not be confirmed as worded: OpenAI's consumer Terms of Use returned HTTP 403 in this run, and the API page that did open sets no flat 13+ bar. It says personal data of children under 13 must not be processed without zero data retention and that COPPA applies. Keeping kids off the cloud stays the family's rule; store:false was not shown to count as zero data retention.
unverified: Llama Guard 3 as the classifier is the roadmap's choice and appears nowhere in the installed OpenClaw docs (its Ollama library page is cited under G019).
Whether kids admitted by pairing are refused as approvers; the roadmap itself marks this as untested.
How accurate any local classifier is on questions from 8 and 10 year olds; no evaluation exists yet.
'Refuse whole-worksheet answers' is a prompt rule; no source shows a model holds to it when a child pushes.
A parent asking the same questions from their own chat works today, but that is the parent using the cloud model, not the child.
Whether the Apple on-device model can be called from a host job for an ad hoc summary; the doc gives it an 8,192-token window and 1,024 output tokens and describes utility use only.
Reading the per-agent database from a command job (read-only open or the history RPC) was not tried.

Which session transcript a delivered digest line is copied into: the installed source appends direct scheduled deliveries to a session transcript (dist/delivery-dispatch-awareness-CcGkYFaV.mjs:518), and if that session belongs to a parent's cloud-backed agent, the quoted kid text would reach a cloud model.
Whether ChatGPT's controls changed after the September 2025 launch report; OpenAI's own page returned 403 in this run.
How the plugin sends a proactive message to the parents from inside a hook; G009 covers the agent `message` tool and host jobs, and no plugin-side send path was found in the hook docs read.
Which Home Assistant conversation integration can target a custom OpenAI-compatible endpoint in 2026 (the roadmap cites a community one; I did not verify it).
Whisper latency inside a VM on this Mac.
Whether OpenClaw can issue an HTTP credential scoped to one agent.

Whether a trusted-proxy identity in front of the HTTP endpoint could narrow a caller to one agent. With the token auth this gateway uses, the docs say scope headers are ignored and the request's model field selects any agent.
safety: No cloud call touches kid content: the agent, its classifiers and the digest summariser are local, and with the classifier down the agent answers 'ask a grown-up'. Alerts carry a category, not the child's words. The riskier part is the speaker's bridge: the chat endpoint is equivalent to an operator secret, so the speaker must reach only the tool-less kids agent.

name: Scheduled-jobs registry in family.json5: per-person switches, a charter per job, failure guardrails
description: Every scheduled feature becomes a named switch per person in one reviewed file. From that entry the generator creates the job with a time limit and a tool cap and writes a short charter the parents can read: what Happy may do without asking, what needs a yes first, when to stop and ask, what it must never do. Failure alerts are routed to Tony instead of the family; a job that keeps failing stops itself, and whether that last notice reaches Tony or the job owner's thread is still to be checked; recurring runs missed during a power cut are skipped, while one-off reminders still catch up.
example: Turning Jordan's school digest off is a one-line change Tony reviews. The 19:30 brief fails twice in a row: Tony gets one text, and one more when it recovers. After a power cut the 07:00 brief does not turn up at 11:40.
how: gen-family reads the family.json5 flags and emits `openclaw automations add/edit/remove`, keyed on the stable `--name`, with `--agent`, `--to`, `--tz`, `--announce`, `--timeout-seconds` and an explicit `--tools` cap on every job; it diffs against `automations list --all --json`, because the default list hides disabled jobs. The same entries render one `## Program: <name>` section per job (Authority, Trigger, Approval gate, Escalation, What NOT to do, plus an execute-verify-report rule) into templates/person/AGENTS.md, and each job message points at its program instead of repeating it; isolated jobs must not use `--light-context`, which drops the bootstrap files. Gateway config: a global `cron.failureAlert` object routed to the operator's handle; `cron.skipMissedJobs: true`; `cron.triggers.enabled: false`. These three switches are plain config and can go in before the generator exists; triggers must be off before timed reminders (F007) or any other item gives an agent the `automations` tool. happy-inspect reads `automations list --all` to catch auto-disabled jobs. The healthchecks dead-man switch stays the only signal for a Mac that is off.
caveats: A charter is prompt text, not enforcement; the hard limits stay in tool policy and hooks.

AGENTS.md shares a bootstrap budget (20,000 characters per file by default); keep each program to about ten lines. Scheduled runs do not get MEMORY.md, so anything a program needs must be in AGENTS.md, the job message or a tool result.
A chat instruction does not change a charter; it waits for a reviewed deploy.
By default a failure alert goes to the failing job's own announce target, so Jordan would get 'job failed' texts for her jobs unless they are rerouted to Tony.
Alerts start after 2 failures in a row with a 1-hour cooldown. A recurring job is switched off after 10 failures in a row and then disappears from the default job list.
Without a per-job timeout an isolated agent job is bounded only by a 60-minute watchdog.
After a reboot with FileVault locked nothing fires and nothing alerts. One-shot reminders still catch up after an outage even with skipMissedJobs set.

Jobs an agent creates in chat, once

-main holds the automations tool, are outside the registry, so the diff must tolerate or report them.

With triggers on, trigger scripts and script payloads run with the owning agent's full tool policy, exec included. Switching triggers off also switches off the trigger-script design of F029 until that is deliberately turned back on.
corrections: Diffing against 'automations list --json' is not enough: the list shows enabled jobs only unless --all is passed, so a job disabled by a mute would look missing and be created twice. Use 'automations list --all --json'.
unverified: Whether gen-family, run from Tony's admin account, can reach the happy user's Gateway with the admin operator scope the docs require.
Whether scheduler-sent failure alerts pass through the G009 recipient-pin hook or bypass it.
Where the auto-disable notice lands: the docs say the owning agent receives it even when failure alerts are off, so it may reach the family member's thread instead of Tony's.
safety: Purely restrictive. Charters narrow behaviour and grant nothing; never-list items are written under What NOT to do and are also unreachable by tool policy. Alert text shown in chat is a normalized cause, and routing alerts to the operator keeps one person's job details out of another person's thread.

From AUT-08 (Unattended-job guardrails (failure alerts, auto-disable, missed runs)): Carry over: the global `cron.failureAlert` routed to Tony, `--timeout-seconds` and a `--tools` cap on every job, `cron.skipMissedJobs: true`, `cron.triggers.enabled: false` before any agent is given the automations tool, happy-inspect watching for auto-disabled jobs, and the caveats on alert thresholds, the 60-minute watchdog and one-shot catch-up. The three gateway switches can be set today, ahead of the generator, and triggers must be off before F007 hands any agent the automations tool.
